name: Is it cheaper to convert a garage or build a new ADU?

mainEntity.name: Which usually costs less in Los Angeles County: converting an existing garage or starting with a new detached ADU?
mainEntity.text: Which usually costs less in Los Angeles County: converting an existing garage or starting with a new detached ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most cases, converting an existing garage is the lower-cost path because you are preserving major parts of the building shell. That can reduce excavation, framing, roofing, and sometimes exterior finish expenses. However, the cost advantage can narrow if the garage is in poor condition or needs substantial upgrades to meet living-space standards. Hidden repairs, utility upgrades, and fire or energy compliance work can add up quickly. A new detached ADU costs more upfront but may offer a better long-term outcome if the garage is too small, poorly located, or structurally weak. Homeowners should compare total project value, not just the initial price tag. The right answer depends on condition, layout, and goals such as rental income, privacy, or resale appeal. A careful side-by-side estimate is the best way to decide.
acceptedAnswer.description: Garage conversions usually cost less than new detached ADUs because the foundation, walls, and roof already exist. The savings can shrink if the garage needs major structural, electrical, plumbing, or slab work to become a code-compliant living unit.
